change.title: pr-33832-flat
change.description: Add AuthzClientCryptoProvider for authorization client cryptographic operations
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Several providers on the classpath no longer fail; ties are resolved silently by classpath order
findings.body:
The old code threw `IllegalStateException` when more than one `CryptoProvider` was found. The new code sorts by `order()` and takes the first one. `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider` and `FIPS1402Provider` all return 200 (crypto/default DefaultCryptoProvider.java:82-85, crypto/elytron WildFlyElytronProvider.java:75-78, crypto/fips1402 FIPS1402Provider.java:113-116). Each has its own `META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider` file. If two of them end up on the classpath, for example the default BC provider next to the FIPS one, the winner is whichever `ServiceLoader` lists first, because `sorted` is stable. Before this change that setup failed at startup. Now a server meant to run in FIPS mode can silently run with the non-FIPS provider. The only trace is a `debug` log (lines 64-70).

The ordering is only needed so the order-100 `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` loses to a real provider. Keep the fail-fast when the top two providers have the same `order()`, and log the ignored providers at `warn` or `info` rather than `debug`.

findings.title: `order()` is a new abstract method on a public SPI interface
findings.body: Any `CryptoProvider` outside this repository stops compiling and fails with `AbstractMethodError` at runtime. The four implementations in this repository are all updated. A `default int order() { return 0; }` would keep the SPI compatible, and the in-repo providers could still override it. Related: `CryptoIntegration.java:69` passes a built string to `logger.debugf(String)` as a format string. Use `debug` or pass parameters instead. The message also ends with a trailing ", ".

findings.title: Dead statements in `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`
findings.body: Lines 114-115 build two `ASN1Encoder` instances and discard them. They have no effect and look like leftover debugging. Delete them.

findings.title: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns the JDK's PKCS12 provider, and `CryptoIntegration.init` pins this provider for the whole JVM
findings.body:
`BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` is computed from this method (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/util/BouncyIntegration.java:33-39). It will be the name of whichever provider backs the default KeyStore type, usually `SUN`. Callers such as `FIPS1402Provider.getKeyStore` pass `BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` to `getInstance`, so a mislabelled provider name is a risk.

`AuthzClient.create` now calls `CryptoIntegration.init`, which stores the provider in a static field that is set only once. If `AuthzClient` is the first caller in a JVM where only authz-client's service file is visible, every later `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getSignature/getKeyFactory/getAesCbcCipher/...` throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")`. Please document this limitation on the class. Alternatively, return `null` from `getBouncyCastleProvider`, which `BouncyIntegration` already handles by falling back to the first security provider.

findings.title: Test never exercises ES384/ES512 sizes or long-form DER lengths, and only checks a self round-trip
findings.body:
The key is a default `EC` key (P-256, line 42) and is used for ES256, ES384 and ES512 alike. The signature is therefore always about 70-72 bytes of DER, which uses a short-form length. A real ES512 (P-521) signature is about 138-139 bytes and needs the long-form length (`0x81 xx`). That long-form path is in `ASN1Encoder.writeLength` (line 67-79) and `ASN1Decoder.readLength` (line 137-164), and the test never runs it. The 66-byte r/s values and the leading-zero handling in `integerToBytes` for ES512 are not covered either. For ES384/ES512 with a P-256 key the code only left-pads r and s.

The assertion at line 56 compares `rsConcat` with the output of the same provider's decode-encode-decode. An error that is symmetric between encoder and decoder would still pass. Nothing compares the re-encoded DER with the original `sign`, and nothing checks it with `Signature.verify`.

Generate the key on the matching curve for each algorithm (`secp256r1`, `secp384r1`, `secp521r1`). Assert `assertArrayEquals(sign, asn1Des)` or verify the re-encoded DER. Add a case where r or s has a high bit set or leading zeros, and one where the sequence length is above 127.

The `hamcrest` test dependency added in `authz/client/pom.xml` is also unused by this test.

findings.title: Malformed DER can raise unchecked exceptions instead of `IOException`
findings.body: `readLength()` returns -1 for the indefinite form (line 133-135). `readInteger` then calls `read(-1)`, which throws `NegativeArraySizeException` at line 170. `readTagNumber` masks the tag with 0x1f (line 94), so any class or constructed bits are accepted as `INTEGER`/`SEQUENCE`. Trailing bytes after the sequence are ignored, and `integerToBytes` in the provider silently truncates a value longer than `signLength/2`, or turns a negative integer into garbage. The method contract is `throws IOException`. The only in-repo caller, `ECDSASignatureSignerContext`, feeds it the JDK's own signer output, so there is no exposure today. Reject `length < 0` in `readSequence`/`readInteger` and check the tag class and constructed bit.

contracts.action: AuthzClient.create(Configuration) now calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()) before constructing the client
contracts.equivalent_path: Other entry points that detect a provider call CryptoIntegration.init once at startup. The create() and create(InputStream) overloads all funnel into create(Configuration) at lines 63 and 82, so every public entry point is covered.
contracts.before_after: Before: no crypto init in the authz-client, so any use of CryptoIntegration.getProvider() (ECDSAAlgorithm, KeystoreUtil) threw 'Please init first'. After: init runs on every create() call and is a no-op once the static provider is set (CryptoIntegration.java:30-38). ServiceLoader detection then picks the highest order(), and AuthzClientCryptoProvider (100) loses to any real provider (200).
contracts.visible_effect: ES256/384/512 client assertion signing and KeyStore loading work in the authz-client without BouncyCastle. In a JVM with a real provider on the classpath behaviour is unchanged.
contracts.failure_mode: If ServiceLoader finds nothing, init throws IllegalStateException, which surfaces from AuthzClient.create. If only AuthzClientCryptoProvider is visible, the provider is pinned for the JVM and unsupported operations throw UnsupportedOperationException (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:75-96 and 169-225). With several same-order providers the choice depends on classpath order (see the CryptoIntegration finding).

contracts.action: New ECDSACryptoProvider with a hand-written ASN.1 encoder and decoder in place of the BouncyCastle one
contracts.equivalent_path: crypto/default BCECDSACryptoProvider.concatenatedRSToASN1DER and asn1derToConcatenatedRS, which use DERSequenceGenerator and ASN1InputStream. They are reached through core ECDSAAlgorithm.java:45-51 from ECDSASignatureSignerContext and ECDSASignatureVerifierContext.
contracts.before_after: The encode path copies r and s with a 0 pad byte, builds BigIntegers and emits a DER SEQUENCE, the same as the BC implementation (BCECDSACryptoProvider.java:28-47). The decode path takes r and s from the DER and left-pads or truncates them to signLength/2, as the BC path does through X9IntegerConverter (lines 51-70). The new decoder is stricter on sequence arity (it throws when the size is not 2) and more lenient on tags.
contracts.visible_effect: Signatures produced or verified by the authz-client are the same bytes as with the default provider for well-formed input. The unit test only covers short-form lengths with P-256 keys.
contracts.failure_mode: The encoder does not validate that signature.length equals signLength, so a short input throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. This matches the BC path. ECDSASignatureVerifierContext wraps any Exception in VerificationException (ECDSASignatureVerifierContext.java:32-34). The decoder can throw NegativeArraySizeException for an indefinite length (reported as a finding).

summary:
I read all twelve files in the part and found five issues, none of them blockers. I did not build or run anything.

- **Silent provider choice (fix):** `CryptoIntegration` no longer throws when several providers are on the classpath. The default, elytron and FIPS providers all return order 200, so a tie is settled by classpath order and only logged at debug. A server meant to run in FIPS mode could silently run with the non-FIPS provider.
- **Test coverage (fix):** `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` signs with a P-256 key for all three algorithms, so it never reaches long-form DER lengths or the real ES384/ES512 sizes. It also only checks a round trip through the same provider, so a bug that is symmetric in encoder and decoder would pass.
- **Considers (four findings):**
  - `order()` is a new abstract method on the public `CryptoProvider` interface.
  - `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` has two dead statements at lines 114-115.
  - `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns the JDK provider. `AuthzClient.create` also pins this provider for the whole JVM, so later crypto calls that need a real provider would throw `UnsupportedOperationException`.
  - `ASN1Decoder` can throw an unchecked exception on an indefinite length, and it accepts loose tags.

The encode and decode logic matches the existing BouncyCastle implementation for well-formed input.
